acceptance_predicates.description: Every public ASB command and alias accepts -q/--quiet in any permitted option position and it suppresses ASB human operational output without changing effects, exits, or structured results.

Every ASB-owned user-visible result, diagnostic, status, update, warning, and progress write goes through one configurable output router; project init persists normal level and the default stdout/stderr routing.

quiet, normal, verbose, and debug have documented stable meanings and configuration/CLI precedence; normal is the generated-project default and no level leaks sensitive/private data or changes effects, schemas, or exits.
Every human operational line starts with a documented fixed-width four-cell state token whose meaning is available without color; terminal color follows the specified success/error/warning semantics.
--json emits no human result, diagnostic, status, update, or progress output on stdout or stderr regardless of configured human writers, while preserving the exact versioned JSON and exit contracts.
Quiet does not remove required interactive input or suppress the launched TUI application; it only suppresses ASB lifecycle presentation.
Rendering is concise, plain-text safe when redirected, secret/private-data safe, and leaves raw protocol and terminal ownership contracts intact.

definition_of_done: Contract and parser/router/rendering tests cover every public command family and early error path.
Documentation gives exact behavior for default stdout/stderr routing, configured writers, four output levels, human, quiet, redirected, JSON, interactive, and TUI modes.
Independent review, exact-head checks, signed merge, and exact-main evidence pass.

outputs.description: Closed human status token, color, stream, writer, level, and mode contract.

gates.description: Project-init defaults, configured writer routing, all four levels, and CLI precedence are covered without bypasses or sensitive output.
Quiet and JSON mode tests prove silence while human terminal and redirected renderings retain stable fixed-width state tokens.
Authoritative public command inventory and early error paths are fully covered.
JSON, exits, protocol, privacy, prompt, and TUI ownership contracts remain compatible.
